nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach. The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: This dataset includes empirical data such as vehicle locations extracted from traffic video frames, used to calibrate simulation parameters and as inputs for the DRL method. It provides traffic volumes for the mainline and on-ramp from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. for the simulation in Qingdao and Huangdao, China.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request. No direct URL or DOI is provided.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract Vehicle Locations and Position Matrices
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices. [...] down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle location points are extracted from raw video frames to form position matrices mt for each time step. These matrices are then down-sampled for computational efficiency. The position matrix also includes signal state information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/3 tools named, 1/5 params stated (only final output size provided, not underlying Uv,Ug,Ur).

nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st: St = {mt-(N-1),..., mt}.
nodes_process.description: Consecutive down-sampled position matrices (N of them) are stacked to form the complete DRL state representation for a given time step. This captures vehicle dynamics over time.

nodes_process.source_quote: The ramp meter takes two possible actions at fixed decision time step L to determine whether the phase in the next time step is green (G) or red (R), namely, action set A = {G, R}.
nodes_process.description: Define the discrete action space for the DRL agent, consisting of two signal phases: green (G) and red (R). These actions are decided at fixed time steps.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward rt after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, mu > 0, omega < 0
nodes_process.description: Define the reward function (rt) to guide the DRL agent, calculated based on the average speed (vt) in the merging area and the average queue length (qt) at the on-ramp, with respective positive and negative weights.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/1 tools named, all params stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: Initialize a deep Q-network, a modified version of Mnih et al.'s, consisting of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers followed by two fully connected (FC) layers, each producing a different output (Q-value and speed/queue predictions for multitask learning).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3 (diagram instead of textual layer description), 0/3 tools named, all params stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1. The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update w_i to minimize the loss function.
nodes_process.description: The deep Q-learning (DQL) agent is trained using the Adam optimizer, incorporating techniques like experience replay and a target network for stability. It utilizes a multitask learning strategy with a combined loss function (L1 + λL2) to learn optimal ramp metering policies.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/6 tools named, all params stated. Training frames (10^6) is mentioned but not mapped to (N,T).

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies
nodes_process.description: Implement the Proportional-Integral-based ALINEA (PI-ALINEA) algorithm for ramp metering, which adjusts red phase length using current and previous downstream occupancies, a desired occupancy, and regulator parameters. The green phase length is fixed.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3 (formula given but not full implementation), 0/2 tools named, all params stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Simulate and Evaluate DRL and Baseline
nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Evaluate the trained DRL agent, a 'no-control' scenario, and the PI-ALINEA baseline using the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator. Performance metrics like travel times, queue lengths, and traffic flows are measured over 20 simulation experiments for each scenario. Simulations use real-world traffic data profiles and different random seeds.
tools_mentioned: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU version not stated
Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 3.6 GHz 6 cores version not stated
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/3 tools named (plus hardware info), 2/3 params stated.
